title: Why the record savers save, and what caps them: anatomy, centre, copy wall, helpers
made_with: AI agents (Claude) directed by the author
note: No person has read any proof in this section; nothing in it is checked in Lean. Savings are plain decimals. Figures of the community are its claims as checked by its own programs.

findings.statement: OpenAI's unit, the community's record unit T74 and the Lean-checked U8X0HQ all save by one mechanism: one free direction per data array (crossing slack), delivered through a centre that works like an index code, with junk cancelled along a second route of helpers. The Lean-checked words carry no saving object of their own; their saving is the community's network and helper circuit.
findings.status_detail: the synthesis skeptic confirmed the account of the mechanism and the design figures; the OpenAI and community dissections had no skeptic; the dissection of my words was checked in part

findings.statement: OpenAI's network: paid moves = W*m - 2*(starting-frame directions of data that changes arrays) + 2*(directions the centre drops); the centre takes back 19 % of the gift; carriers are 99.9995 % of the arrays; 25 points instead of 100 would give 4.18e-10.
findings.status_detail: one program each, not repeated by a skeptic; the rule checked by brute force at small sizes
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: family.py, frames_check.py, caps.py and moment_price.py re-run; frames_check prints all identities true for m = 2 to 5; caps.py gives 4.18e-10 at 25 points

findings.statement: In the community's checkpoint files the net free fraction (free directions net of the centre, as a share of all directions) is exactly 4.8924e-3 at every checkpoint from Kothe's atm3 (#588, the circuit Shea checked) to T74, so the whole +4.7 % climb since atm3 is regrouping of the paid work (average child rank 3.44 to 3.95); per call T74 keeps 35.56 free directions of 7,267.6 (0.36 of a move per array).
findings.status_detail: one program on the community's checkpoint profiles, not repeated by a skeptic
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: lineage.py, anatomy.py, caps.py and window.py reproduce their recorded outputs byte for byte (lineage.py re-run again by the section's fact checker, identical)

findings.statement: In the Lean-checked words D = 320 free directions per replica (896 free minus 576 for the centre), 5/14 of a move per data array, the same on all 11 words of the ladder; of the factor 1.318 over Shea's start, 1.032 is the community's better word and 1.277 is Lean-route overhead removed.
findings.status_detail: the build skeptic reproduced D = 320 and the fold root of U8X0HQ with its own code
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: anatomy_ours.py, identity.py, knobs.py and stages.py reproduce their recorded outputs byte for byte

findings.statement: Ceilings inside the community's model: T74's own word with best packing 1.6876e-3 (+0.47 %); every child as large as the 9-direction window 2.88e-3; centre free and every child at the largest rank 3.98e-2; the U8 line at an exact fill 1.6647327e-3; the U8 word with free centres 4.67e-3 (what-if). With one free direction per family, 0.1 needs a block of 28 or less.
findings.status_detail: prices and ceilings of a model computed by a program, not proofs; the first three come from the dissection of T74, which had no skeptic; the build skeptic reproduced the exact-fill price 1.6647327e-3 with its own code; the what-if with free centres was not repeated
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: caps.py, knobs.py, cap.py and capcheck.py reproduce their recorded outputs

findings.statement: The whole crossing class is capped near 3e-3 and no construction in it reaches 0.1.
findings.status_detail: refuted by the synthesis skeptic: under the synthesis's own inputs (112 ports, 3 stages, block 25) the ceiling is about 5.6e-3, and the exclusion of 0.1 rests on a stage-window wall that was argued, not proved

findings.statement: E8 is the best centre among the root systems: copy ratio 0.600 (120 ports, 8 centres, window 9) against 0.643 for the community's 112 ports, 0.778 for E7, 1.167 for E6, 1.0 or more for D_n and A_n.
findings.status_detail: the synthesis skeptic rebuilt the table from scratch; that E8 is best among all two-angle line systems rests on a classification theorem cited from memory (argued)
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: ade.py, clique.py and the skeptic's roots.py reproduce their recorded outputs

findings.statement: Barnes-Wall (BW16), the full Leech set and Coxeter-Todd (real and complex forms) fail as centres: BW16 has 1,304 junk terms per port and a junk clique of at least 53; Leech has a 23-line clique; Coxeter-Todd real has 242 junk per port and a clique of 45, complex has window at least 15, copy ratio at least 0.71 and cube-root phases.
findings.status_detail: the build skeptic and the round-2 skeptic rebuilt BW16 and Coxeter-Todd with their own constructions; every figure matched
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: bw16.py, vbw16.py, ct12.py and vct12.py reproduce their recorded outputs

findings.statement: As units, BW16, BW32, Leech and the Reed-Muller line systems are all worse than E8 per port on both sides: the BW16 complex ceiling at nine stages is 1.2863e-3; a real BW16 bit decoder prices at 9.54e-4 with helpers and 1.38e-3 without, against 1.86e-3 for E8 in the same model.
findings.status_detail: symmetry round; no skeptic report came back

findings.statement: Two-sided slack on the U8 word: the backward calls pay the gain back exactly (224 crossings per backward call, 896 per replica), and the forward calls pay too, so it loses at this gate order.
findings.status_detail: exact crossing counts; one skeptic reproduced them and made the kill stronger
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: calib.py, twosided_local.py and the skeptic's vcalib.py reproduce their recorded outputs

findings.statement: Crossing lemma: no local word with one shared extra line s can beat the same word with s deleted; the best case is a tie at block 74, priced 1.6246236e-3 to 1.6537530e-3, below the one-sided ceiling 1.6647327e-3.
findings.status_detail: checked exhaustively by computer on small cases; one skeptic re-derived it and corrected the author's floor; the deletion step is checked by computer on 120,000 random steps
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: toybfs.py, quotient.py, ct12.py and the skeptic's vproj.py, vprice.py, vbank.py and vmulticall.py reproduce their recorded outputs

findings.statement: Two-sided slack would double the record (x2.03, 3.4e-3); a single-crossing word could reach about 3.2e-3; the single-crossing word is held to D <= 208 per replica.
findings.status_detail: the first killed by the exact build, the second withdrawn after the crossing lemma, the third corrected by the round-2 skeptic to 'a tie at best' (it assumed that no X array holds s between calls)
findings.refuted_by: the two-sided build and the round-2 skeptic

findings.statement: A second line per family (the mirrored line) exists (69,616 twisted variants, all symmetric involutions) and its crossing counts stay below the gain, but cleaning kills it: a scratch array can visit at most 4, 8 or 45 of a total's 56 x's without a paid drop, and the best cleaning scheme known costs 120 per call against a room of 34.
findings.status_detail: dead at first order by about x3.5, argued; no lower bound above 34 is proved for every scheme; the skeptic found and checked the 120-per-call scheme exactly; the lines and their Gram matrix are checked by computer and reproduced by the skeptic; the count of twists and their being involutions are argued by hand, with the key step reproduced by the skeptic; the crossing counts were not re-run by the skeptic
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: lines.py, price.py and the skeptic's v2price.py reproduce their recorded outputs; v5perx.py re-runs its exact check of the 120-per-call scheme (every gate frame-equal, scratch exactly 0)

findings.statement: Cleaning the mirrored line costs at least 272 per call.
findings.status_detail: refuted by the skeptic: 272 was the cost of one greedy scheme, and the skeptic built one at 120

findings.statement: Small-block crossing networks cannot reuse window directions: the block is at least 1 + 2*sigma (13 for E7, 17 for E8 and the 112 ports), in the model of fixed addresses, frames that only grow except at centres, one frame per gate and copies erased against their own source; D4 and A3 save nothing; generous ceilings with one free direction per array stay below 0.04.
findings.status_detail: one skeptic checked each step with its own code; four limits of scope (one-layer centres; natural codes; the bank that sends twice uses shared centres both times; paid work in pieces of at most sigma directions, argued for about half the arrays)
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: designs.py, classfloor.py, early.py, ceiling.py and the skeptic's vdesign.py, vclass.py and vraw.py reproduce their recorded outputs

findings.statement: Crossing networks at blocks 13 to 25 price at most 7.3920e-4 (T74's word, block 25, one bank pair, ideal banks), 7.3057e-4 with the word of the Lean-checked line: x0.44 of T74 and 13.5 times short of 0.01; with junk cleaning free 2.3338e-3; the most generous ceiling at block 25 is 8.2607e-3. Shrinking the template only loses.
findings.status_detail: prices computed by a program; the skeptic reproduced every price to every digit with its own fold
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: price_p112.py, shrink.py, price_t74_p1.py, items.py, natural.py, ceilings.py and the skeptic's vprice.py, vclique.py and vhost.py reproduce their recorded outputs

findings.statement: Centre floors for decoders that gather, drop once and scatter: D5, D6, A4 and A5 exactly 0.8 per port per call (they never save with one or two bank pairs); E7 at least 35 per call; the 112 ports at least 52.36; E8 at least 54.45. Free meetings clean at most 58 % of the 112-port junk and 44 % of E7's.
findings.status_detail: a counting argument with its numbers computed by a program; the skeptic rebuilt the floors of D5, D6, A4, A5 and E7 with its own code, without building labels, and found them stronger than stated; for the 112 ports and E8 it upheld the argument but did not recompute the numbers; the centre round later recomputed 52.36 exactly with two programs; 54.45 has not been recomputed; the free-meeting bound is argued and upheld in its scope
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: cliquefloor.py reproduces every design it computes by default; vclique.py reproduces its output

findings.statement: The x0.44 at medium blocks comes from the missing idle levels; medium blocks are closed for the record.
findings.status_detail: refuted by the skeptic: the x0.44 is mostly the centre's share of each call (x0.52), hosting only x0.84; the skeptic found template points at blocks 16 and 22, and the block-22 point is open

findings.statement: No single-layer decoder of the community's 112 ports that keeps today's junk (delivered table of rank 8) costs less than 64 per call under the shipped charge, for any number of terms built anywhere.
findings.status_detail: a written proof whose counting steps and last cases are checked by computer (exhaustive covers); one skeptic re-derived the rewriting step by hand, recomputed every computed input and checked the list of slices by a separate argument, and found no gap; it takes the community's rank-8 rescaling theorem (#1212, #1815) as given; for the community's own centre the shipped charge rests on one sentence of its text
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: calib.py (64 and 72 found), negctl.py (48 refused, 2,333 violations), nd.py, profiles.py (survivors m = 9 to 12, identical to the brute force of xcheck.py), coflat.py, coflats_all.py, m9.py, cover3.py and the rest listed in programs/README.md reproduce their recorded outputs

findings.statement: Every single-layer decoder of the 112 ports costs at least 52.36 per call (a count over the 1,260 orthogonal frames); a weighted count gives 59.0733 for decoders that keep today's junk, superseded by finding 19.
findings.status_detail: two independent programs each
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: onesided.c reproduces its recorded output (52.3636 per call) byte for byte

findings.statement: Under the pairing charge (projected copies, which the community's checker forbids) no counting floor above 16.9 exists.
findings.status_detail: reproduced by the skeptic, whose own cruder search showed that the count can give at most 20.1

findings.statement: Relays (a target reading another target's register) never beat the static copy floor, in any order, any number of rounds, scalar or vector, over any field, in the frame game.
findings.status_detail: upheld by two skeptics; also checked by computer with SAT (rank 8 impossible with relays on P120 and P111, re-run on the true bit puncture); relies on the community's frame-sandwich rule, which it marks as argued

findings.statement: Theorem A (bit side): every F_2 star decoder whose read span contains the label space and has dimension at most 11 costs at least 63 (at least 64 at dimension 10); every decoder with 9 or fewer totals has such a span.
findings.status_detail: exact, on both punctures; upheld by both skeptics within that scope (one skeptic's own encoding confirmed the true puncture at 9 or fewer totals; the other's did not finish in 20 minutes)

findings.statement: Complex side: any decoder on P112 costs at least 53 (octad count); natural decoders cost at least 64 and only the community's reaches it; on all of E8 (P120) natural decoders need 72.
findings.status_detail: exact and exhaustive; one program each, not repeated by a skeptic; the 53 rests on a one-line rank argument (every octad needs 8 different totals) followed by an exact count over all subspaces
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: copyfloor.py e8 reproduces its calibration (72, 63, 64) byte for byte

findings.statement: Every decoder on the full E8 unit (P120) needs at least 55 copy moves.
findings.status_detail: 10 October 2026; the same kind of octad count as the 53 on P112, with its counts computed by a program (an exhaustive enumeration of subspaces); no skeptic has read it

findings.statement: The isotropic-cut proof and the stage hand-over proof of the copy wall.
findings.status_detail: both refuted as proofs by both of their skeptics; what survives is an exact counting lemma: with 9 or more totals, any mix of isotropic line cuts and full-width star totals costs at least 64 (certificate checked on all 255 cuts)

findings.statement: The copy-wall round's plan: deciding the octad Hall test (each octad's 8 ports matched to 8 different totals) for the three cost-63 shapes would either close them or give the first family of frames worth decoding.
findings.status_detail: refuted by a counterexample of the symmetry round: a cost-63 family of 9 frames of dimension 7 passes the test on all 1,260 octads yet fails on 21 other maximal cliques and is not a decoder; counting over all 1,996 maximal cliques gives only 52; no skeptic report came back for that round

findings.statement: Stage sharing: frames are shared iff labels are orthogonal (6,470 of 12,210 pairs); in an exact two-stage toy every word needs at least 18 paid moves and riders with cleanup cost 18 or 21; the permutation door fails at the stage boundary (all 32 tiny pairs, all 6,470 pairs of the #589 geometry), and its cheapest repair costs exactly as much as the standard copies, so it saves nothing.
findings.status_detail: each track had a skeptic with independent code; the toy is too small to show a gain of any kind (an earlier lemma rules out every saving there), so riders are closed inside the toy only, not at the community's scale; the skeptic of the door found a cheaper repair than the author's (+8 over the standard copies): it costs 168 moves on the tiny unit, the same as the standard copies, against the plain word's 160
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: swapdoor.py and replay.py reproduce their recorded outputs byte for byte

findings.statement: In the community's cover-of-charts construction no total can cross any of the five stage boundaries: a total's 56 ports continue into 56 different invocations; paying to re-route costs at least 220 moves per total per boundary against 8 for the star copy.
findings.status_detail: checked against the community's own boundary files (120 ports, 1,080 stage translations); the small case h = 3, m = 5 checked exhaustively by computer; no skeptic report came back
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: small_case.py re-run: part A reproduced exactly; parts C (the whole cover O(7,2), 1,451,520 invocations) and B (h = 4, m = 7) ran to completion with no counter-case; the recorded output of C covered a sample of 2,001 invocations; re-run again by the section's fact checker with the same result (276 s, 13 MB)

findings.statement: Adding one port raises the copy cost by at most 1, so cost(P120) >= 72 would give at least v - 48 for every punctured unit.
findings.status_detail: argued by one agent; no skeptic has read it

findings.statement: The 504 complex-side helpers per call of the U8 word are 392 plane visitors, meeting Scholz's packet-plane bound exactly, and 112 M copies; the integer programme reproduces 36 per block, so 504 is optimal in the community's visit model. On the k8 word: 480 = 368 + 112.
findings.status_detail: the census was reproduced by a skeptic on both words

findings.statement: None of the 504 complex-side helpers is removed by narrower ends (exact no for all 378 full-width helpers), half reads (0 of 168), one helper for two planes (0 pairs) or Walsh packets; bit exits are impossible.
findings.status_detail: narrower ends and bit exits upheld by skeptics (narrower ends stronger than stated); half reads, two planes and the Walsh-packet confirmation of the symmetry round had no skeptic

findings.statement: One bit-side carrier (470) retires in a word that passes the community's bit checker, worth +0.012 % to +0.119 % on c; kappa does not move.
findings.status_detail: checked with the community's checker; no skeptic ran and the hosting step was not re-run, so the price is a range

findings.statement: Shared pair rows remove 56 helpers on U8 (448 instead of 504), and 32 to 40 on k8.
findings.status_detail: refuted by both skeptics on U8 (the model charged U8 for work it does free, left out the M copies, and its recipe breaks the frame rule) and by the k8 skeptic (like for like the model is worse, 448 against 368 in-block helpers)

findings.statement: The rank-7 helper pair 580/581 on the k8 word is unclaimed by any contributor.
findings.status_detail: refuted by the skeptic: Thomas DiFiore's #1148 had already claimed 580 and 581 with six more, as a strict superset with a higher figure; the both-pairs assembly (with Kothe's 574 and 575, on his #1121 owner map repacked by my agents) passed the community's admission pipeline at kappa 1.673020532e-3, reproduced by the skeptic, but adds nothing new; nothing was posted

findings.statement: The 112 M copies need at least 8 relays per group.
findings.status_detail: refuted as stated: every target already holds all 64 packet sources after the cut, so the M copies cancel content rather than deliver it; the floor holds only with the centre values and the cut held fixed

findings.statement: No decoder of the 112 ports invariant under a symmetry of order 7 or 8 costs 63 or less: about 8.7 billion frame families fail exact necessary tests while 21 cost-64 controls pass; the best per Hamming block is 28, the community's.
findings.status_detail: no skeptic report came back; orders 4 and 3 not finished

findings.statement: The k8 word cannot be improved by local rewrites: its frames are exactly optimal at its gate order, and with commuting gates reordered it is optimal for dependency gaps up to 4 (98 % of the gates); at gap 5 at most 1.66 cost units (about 1.3e-7 of kappa) are not excluded.
findings.status_detail: integer programmes; no skeptic report came back
